title: Project registry (projects.yml)
description: Checked in pre-commit and CI. Rules that span several projects (a name used once per server; unique hostnames, titles and deploy keys; a project domain that is in domains, a project server that is in servers) or several fields (health inside paths, a name in both env and secrets) are checked by the playbook (roles/projects/tasks/validate.yml); Terraform checks subdomains too.

domains.description: Every domain the servers answer for, each a Cloudflare zone. The first one holds the status page (status.<domain>) and is the default domain of every project. Unique names are checked by the playbook and Terraform.

servers.description: Every server (Droplet), by its hostname, which Ansible's inventory uses too. The first one is the default server of every project, and serves the status page. Unique names, each under a domain in domains, are checked by the playbook and Terraform.

domain_name.description: A lowercase domain of two labels or more, such as abrunacci.dev or example.com.ar.

mail_forward.description: Local parts Cloudflare Email Routing forwards to the inbox in terraform/.env (TF_VAR_email_forward_to).

proton.description: Proton Mail hosts the domain's mail (MX, SPF and the verification TXT, terraform/email.tf).

verification.description: The value Proton shows for the domain's TXT record, after protonmail-verification=.

dkim.description: The part Proton's three DKIM CNAMEs share: protonmail.domainkey.<dkim>.domains.proton.ch. Shown once the domain is verified.

not.description: A domain has one set of MX records: Email Routing's or Proton's.

name.description: The server's hostname, such as server.abrunacci.dev: a name under one of the domains (Terraform creates its A/AAAA records there).

database.description: Where its projects' databases are: local, PostgreSQL in a container on the server (the default), or managed, the managed cluster Terraform creates for it (terraform/production.tf), reached over the VPC through a PgBouncer pool, with TLS verify-full.

ssh.description: How SSH reaches it: public (port 22, the default), or tailscale, only on the Tailscale interface.

max_cpus.description: The most CPUs one backend container on it may have, from 0.1 to 2. Defaults to 1.

name.description: Directories, registry entry and, with a database, the database and user (with - turned into _). Used once per server: a project on two servers is two entries with the same name, each with its own server (checked by the playbook).

domain.description: One of the domains in domains (checked by the playbook and Terraform). Without it, the first one.

server.description: The server the project runs on: one of the names in servers (checked by the playbook and Terraform). Without it, the first one. Its DNS records point there, and only that server's playbook run deploys it.

subdomain.description: DNS record (Terraform) and Caddy site, under the project's domain. "@" is the domain itself, and also gets www redirected to it. Without one, the project is internal: no DNS record, no Caddy site, and only a backend.

redirect_from.description: Other hostnames that send visitors here with a permanent redirect (301), keeping the path and query string, such as another domain the project goes by. Each one is a domain in domains or a name under one (Terraform creates its A/AAAA records there). Unique hostnames are checked by the playbook and Terraform. Only with a subdomain.

also_serves.description: Other hostnames that serve the same site and backend as the project's own, with no redirect, such as a second name for the same app. Each one is a domain in domains or a name under one (Terraform creates its A/AAAA records there), with noindex: true to send X-Robots-Tag: noindex on that name only. Unique hostnames are checked by the playbook and Terraform. Only with a subdomain.

noindex.description: Search engines must not list the site under this name (X-Robots-Tag: noindex, nofollow).
Search engines must not list the site under the project's own name (X-Robots-Tag: noindex, nofollow), such as a demo. Its also_serves names say so each on their own. Only with a subdomain.

title.description: Shown on the placeholder page, and the project's group on the status page, so unique among the projects with a subdomain (checked by the playbook). Defaults to name.

repo.description: Linked from the placeholder page. Optional: leave it out for private repositories.

database.description: A PostgreSQL database and user for the backend. The playbook never drops it: while it exists on the server, removing the project or setting false fails the playbook until it is retired by hand (ansible/README.md).

permissions_policy.description: The Permissions-Policy header of the site and its backend, replacing roles/caddy's default (caddy_permissions_policy, which turns off the camera, microphone, location and other powerful features). Write the whole policy, such as "camera=(self), microphone=(), geolocation=()": each feature off (()), for the site itself ((self)), or for any origin (*). Only with a subdomain.

referrer_policy.description: The Referrer-Policy header of the site and its backend, replacing roles/caddy's default (strict-origin-when-cross-origin, which the backend may replace): set here, the backend cannot replace it. Only with a subdomain.

content_security_policy.description: The whole Content-Security-Policy header of the site and its backend, replacing roles/caddy's default (frame-ancestors 'none', which the backend may replace): set here, the backend cannot replace it. Directives separated by "; ", such as "default-src 'self'; frame-ancestors 'none'". It must keep frame-ancestors, so no other site may frame the page, and has no double quotes, backslashes or braces (Caddy would read {...} as a placeholder). Only with a subdomain.

deploy_key.description: Public ed25519 key of the project's CI. Its authorized_keys line is fixed to deploying this project only: its site, its backend or both. Without it, the project cannot be deployed.

allOf.description: Without a subdomain, nothing is public: no domain, no site, and a backend Caddy does not reach, so it has no port, health path, paths or private paths (the image's own HEALTHCHECK says whether it is healthy).
With a subdomain, Caddy reaches the backend on its port and checks its health path.
At least one component: a site or a backend.
Only a backend can use a database. Its roles are named after the project plus _app, which PostgreSQL limits to 63 characters.
Migrations and a database URL scheme need a database.
With a site, the backend only gets the paths listed.
Without a site, the backend gets every path.

image.description: Image repository without a tag or digest, such as ghcr.io/abrunacci/epb-stock-backend. CI sends the digest of each deploy, and the server records it.

port.description: Port it listens on, for Caddy. Only with a subdomain.

health.description: Health check path, with the prefix: Caddy does not strip it. Checked from Caddy's container after each deploy; any 2xx answer is healthy. Only with a subdomain.

paths.description: Caddy path matchers sent to the backend, such as /api/*.

private_paths.description: Caddy path matchers of the backend that the internet must never reach, such as /api/ingest: Caddy answers them 404, even inside paths. Only containers that share a network with the backend may call them. Only with a subdomain.

env.description: Non-secret environment variables, public like the rest of this file. Values are strings: quote numbers and booleans.

secrets.description: Secret environment variables: only their names are here, the values live on the server. generated: created once on the server (64 hex characters). fernet: the same, as a Fernet key (32 random bytes in URL-safe base64, 44 characters), for a backend that encrypts data with it; never rotated, since what it encrypted could no longer be read. manual: set by the admin with project-secret. optional: like manual, but the backend also runs without it (no value, no variable). {from: PROJECT, key: KEY}: the value of another project's secret, copied by the server, which also gives this backend a private network to that project's backend (link-PROJECT).

migrate.description: Command that applies the migrations, run in a one-off container of the new image before each deploy switches to it, such as [alembic, upgrade, head]. It gets MIGRATION_DATABASE_URL and APP_DB_USER.

database_url_scheme.description: Scheme of DATABASE_URL and MIGRATION_DATABASE_URL, such as postgresql+psycopg for SQLAlchemy with psycopg 3. Defaults to postgresql.

memory.description: Memory limit of the container, as a whole percentage of its server's RAM from 1% to 90%, such as "20%": the playbook turns it into MiB on each run (never below 64 MiB), so it follows a resized Droplet. A server's limits add up to memory_max_share at most (ansible/group_vars, 90%; checked by the playbook).

max_body.description: Largest request body Caddy passes to the backend, in KB or MB, such as 64KB for a form. Larger ones get 413 without reaching it. Defaults to 10MB. Only with a subdomain.

client_ip_header.description: A request header Caddy sets to the visitor's address before passing the request on, replacing any value the visitor sent, such as CF-Connecting-IP for a backend that reads the visitor there. Only with a subdomain.

cpus.description: CPU limit of the container, in CPUs, from 0.1 to its server's max_cpus (1 unless the server says otherwise; checked by the playbook). Defaults to 0.5.

worker.description: A second process of the same image, without a port, such as a jobs queue: its own container (backend-PROJECT-worker), started, deployed and rolled back with the backend, always on the same release. It gets the backend's env, DATABASE_URL if the project has a database, the secrets it lists in secrets, which the backend then no longer gets, and the ones in shared_secrets, which both get. Its network only reaches the internet (and the project's database): neither Caddy nor any backend reaches it. Deploys, rollbacks and restarts wait for its health command, as for the backend's health path.

command.description: The process to run instead of the image's own command, such as [python, -m, app.jobs].

health.description: Its HEALTHCHECK, run inside the worker's container every 5 s while it starts, then every 5 minutes, with 60 s to finish: exit 0 while it is working. Deploys wait for it, and the status page gets a heartbeat (PROJECT / Worker) that alerts when it fails.

memory.description: Memory limit of the worker's container, a share of its server's RAM like the backend's memory, apart from it.

cpus.description: CPU limit of the worker's container, apart from the backend's, from 0.1 to its server's max_cpus (checked by the playbook). Defaults to the backend's cpus.

stop_grace_period.description: How long it gets to stop after SIGTERM before it is killed, from 1s to 120s. Defaults to 20s, the backend's.

secrets.description: Names of the backend's secrets that only the worker gets (generated, fernet, manual or optional; not linked ones). They are still set with project-secret, on the project.

shared_secrets.description: Names of the backend's secrets that the worker also gets, while the backend keeps them (generated, fernet, manual or optional; not linked ones, and none of secrets). They are still set with project-secret, on the project.

log_alerts.description: Log lines of the backend to be emailed about (log-alerts, every 5 minutes, one email per run). The lines are emailed as they were logged: only match lines without personal data. Rule names are unique within the backend: checked by the playbook.

log_alert.description: A line matches when every pattern in match is found in it.

name.description: Shown in the email's subject, such as jump_confirmed.

match.description: Python regular expressions, each searched anywhere in the line. Single-quote them in YAML, so backslashes stay as written.

note.description: What the line means and whether anything must be done: the email's first line.

subject.description: How to build the email's subject from the line: a Python regular expression with named groups, and a format that uses them as {group}. A line it does not fit gets the generic subject, PROJECT: NAME, and is emailed all the same.

secret_link.description: Another project's secret, by project name and key. That project must have a backend with a port, and declare the key as generated or manual: checked by the playbook.

command.description: A command as a list of arguments, run without a shell.

env_name.description: An environment variable name. The ones the infrastructure sets itself (per-project databases) are reserved.
